map.name: ISIS Neutron and Muon Source — Rutherford Appleton Laboratory campus and target-station buildings

summary.plain: The Rutherford Appleton Laboratory campus in Oxfordshire, drawn to scale with the two buildings that house ISIS Target Station 1 and Target Station 2. The 163-metre proton synchrotron and the KARMEN neutrino detector site could not be placed from public sources.

unlocated.backlog: Needs the surveyed positions of the ISIS target and proton beam axis in site coordinates (an ISIS/RAL civil drawing or a KARMEN technical paper with a site plan), then the sourced 17.7 m / 100 degree offset places the detector. Until then the KARMEN bunker cannot be located.
unlocated.reason: KARMEN sat 17.7 m from the ISIS target at 100 degrees to the proton beam (KARMEN detector description). The ISIS target and beam direction have no sourced coordinates, the site point is campus-grade (1500 m), and the KARMEN bunker was a 1990-2001 installation that no fetched source or OSM element places; a position derived from the campus point would be invented geometry.

unlocated.backlog: A document that names the building of the synchrotron (and of the linac and the extracted proton beam tunnels): an ISIS site plan with a legend, a Harwell/STFC estates building register, an ISIS design or safety report, or a tender notice that describes the 'synchrotron hall' by building number; then take that building from OSM by its R-number (the OSM names carry them), and add a length check only if the document gives a ring size. A circle may be drawn only if a source states the ring's centre or its hall; the sourced 163 m / 52 m figures fix the radius, not the centre. Leads, unconfirmed: R6 (OSM way 200338539) and R5.3.
unlocated.reason: ISIS proton synchrotron (163 m circumference, 800 MeV, 50 Hz rapid-cycling, per IPAC 2014; 'a 52 m diameter proton synchrotron', CERN Courier 2000), its 70 MeV linac and the extracted proton beamlines to TS1 and TS2. OpenStreetMap maps no ring, tunnel or machine hall for ISIS. The STFC campus map (v2.3, 2022) and OSM both label a cluster of numbered buildings between the two target stations (R5.1-R5.5, R6, R6A; R6 is OSM way 200338539, 4 611 m2; R5.3 is drawn with a rounded north end), but neither says what any of them holds: the ISIS safety page names only R55 (Target Station 1) and R80 (Target Station 2), and searches of ISIS, STFC and JACoW material for 'R6', 'R5.x' with 'synchrotron', 'linac' or 'Front End Test Stand' found no statement of the machine hall's building number. No candidate was drawn: a 52 m ring fits in several of them, which is a reason to find the source, not to guess. The Atlas has no accelerator record for the synchrotron.
